unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Zvi Elimelekh of Dinov, while rabbi of Munkatch, persuades R. Zvi of Zhidachov to travel to Hungary despite his fear, citing the sign of the scar on the nobleman's forehead.
unit.boundary_note: linked to the previous division (refers back to the sign on the nobleman's forehead told there), but forms its own episode

stories.start_quote: והנה הסימן על מצח השר הגיד
stories.summary_en: When the Dinover rabbi, then rabbi of Munkatch, asked R. Zvi to come to Hungary, R. Zvi was afraid, because he blamed his only son's death on an earlier journey there; he asked for a sign, and the Dinover named the scar on the nobleman's forehead, which R. Zvi admitted he had made; only when the Dinover took responsibility for his household in Zhidachov did R. Zvi agree to go.

tags.why: R. Zvi fears the journey to Hungary
his dead son and his household are at stake

the Dinover knows a hidden sign he could not have known by ordinary means
the story turns on the tzaddik's journey to Hungary
the episode is an interaction between two tzaddikim
the tzaddik's power to take responsibility for others
